title: Glint
description: Glass towers seen from the bottom of a Toronto street, straight up into a summer sky, and the pointer is the sun. Move it and the sun's mirror image runs across the curtain walls on the far side of the street, pane by pane, each pane catching it a moment apart because no curtain wall is flat: every pane sits a fraction of a degree off its neighbours and bows with the air sealed inside it. The walls that turn toward the sun warm up and the ones that turn away go into shade, the bright sky round the sun and the sunward edges of the cumulus follow it, in the sky and in every reflection of the sky, and behind a tower the sun is just a rim of light. At the photographer's sun it is the photograph.
intent: Reality pieces: take one real photograph apart into what it is made of and light it again, so the light can move. Summer-film genre (factory/reality/genre-spec.md), herb's worm's-eye reference. One photograph is read as geometry and materials (camera from its vanishing point and its lines, each tower face a plane squared up by rectifying it onto itself, the curtain-wall grid measured in that rectified frame, per-pane normal jitter, albedo, roughness, the sky unprojected to a dome) and relit live: mirror reflection of the sun with Fresnel, through each pane's own normal, plus the sun-dependent part of the sky in the reflections, Lambert sun on frames and walls, developed through the shared film kit. References: real specular glare off curtain walls (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtain_wall_(architecture)), insulated glass pillowing (https://www.glassonweb.com/article/what-causes-distortion-reflections-insulating-glass), Fresnel (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresnel_equations). ?sun=x,y holds the sun (0..1 of the print), ?sun=photo the photographer's, ?still=1 skips the reveal, ?film=0 shows the frame before the film.

sources.author: Davi Rezende (@davirezende)
